Position Description

JOB DESCRIPTION

Would you like to have a career with a collaborative, diverse, and dynamic mining company? We have an exciting opportunity for you!

Barrick is looking for a Geospatial Data & GIS Solutions Lead. The successful candidate is responsible for supporting and advancing geospatial data, GIS, remote sensing, data integration and technical automation capabilities across Exploration. The role works at the intersection of geoscience, GIS, remote sensing, data management and development, helping ensure geological, geochemical, geophysical, remote-sensing and other Exploration datasets are appropriately captured, organized, integrated, quality-controlled, accessible and reusable.

The role combines strong geospatial expertise with hands-on technical development, including the use of Python and geospatial technologies to improve, automate and standardize workflows. Working closely with the Regional Geosciences Data & Analytics Manager and multidisciplinary Exploration teams, the role will help strengthen data standards and knowledge continuity, integrate GIS with other Exploration systems, and develop practical, reusable solutions. The successful candidate is not expected to be an expert in every technology; the role requires a strong geospatial and technical foundation, hands-on Python capability, collaborative problem solving and a strong orientation toward continuous learning. This position is located in Toronto, Canada. The yearly salary for this position is between CAD 119,000 – 133,000.

At Barrick, our vision is to be the world’s most valued gold mining business by finding, developing, and operating the best assets with the best people. We are committed to a safe work environment sending every person home safe and healthy every day and leaving a sustainable legacy on our host communities.

Responsibilities

Work with geological, geochemical, geophysical, remote-sensing and other Exploration datasets across GIS, databases, project environments and web-based platforms.
Support and improve workflows using ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Enterprise, ArcGIS Online, Web GIS, Field Maps and Survey123.

Use approved AI-assisted development tools responsibly where they can improve development, learning, documentation or workflow efficiency.
Work directly with geologists, geochemists, geophysicists, GIS/geoscience data specialists, data engineers and analytics/development resources to understand requirements and co-create practical solutions.
Document datasets, systems and workflows; support knowledge transfer so important technical knowledge is reusable and understood by the broader team.
Support field and office-based Exploration workflows and travel to projects or regional offices as required.
Promote continuous improvement in GIS, geospatial data management, integration and automation practices.
Comply with Barrick Health & Safety, Code of Conduct, Human Rights, Environmental and Community Relations requirements and applicable company policies.

Academic degree in Geography, GIS/Geomatics, Geospatial Science, Remote Sensing, Computer Science, Geoscience, Geological Engineering, Surveying or a related technical discipline required
Strong understanding of GIS and geospatial data concepts and practices, with hands-on experience using professional GIS technologies, preferably the Esri ecosystem required
Experience working with both vector and raster geospatial datasets, including remote sensing, satellite imagery or raster processing required
Hands-on Python programming experience, preferably applied to geospatial data processing, analysis, automation or development preferred
Strong understanding of coordinate systems, projections, spatial data quality, QA/QC and sound data-management practices preferred
Experience compiling, managing, standardizing or integrating geospatial datasets preferred
Strong analytical and practical problem-solving skills, including the ability to understand existing workflows and user needs before selecting a technical solution preferred
Ability to communicate and collaborate effectively with technical and non-technical users across multidisciplinary Exploration teams preferred
Strong orientation toward continuous learning and improvement; ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with the broader team preferred
Valuable but not all required: ArcPy, SQL/SQL Server, spatial databases, APIs, FME/ETL, Git, Azure DevOps, ArcGIS Enterprise/Online, Web GIS, Field Maps, Survey123, cloud geospatial technologies, data pipelines, Leapfrog, Geosoft, Power BI, geoscience/mining data, machine learning or AI-assisted development preferred
Experience in mineral exploration, mining, geology, geophysics, geochemistry, remote sensing or natural resources is highly valuable; strong candidates from other geospatial or scientific backgrounds preferred
Eligible to live and work in the applicable country required
Availability for occasional travel to Exploration projects and regional offices required

jobs.description:
About Peraton

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world's leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we're keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Program Overview

The program is an IDIQ contract for an AWS-based cloud hosting system. Currently, Peraton is supporting the Cloud Security, IoT, and AIML use cases for the environment in a hybrid work environment with Federal employees. Peraton also support the following applications as part of the environment: Dremio, Tableau, Globus, Posit/RStudio, Atlassian, ThingLogix, Alteryx and CloudCheckr.

About The Role

Peraton's Department of the Interior (DOI), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), and NOAA's National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) have identified a critical gap in the federal government's ability to conduct comprehensive Endangered Species Act (ESA) research. While FWS operates an authoritative web-based platform for managing data for terrestrial and freshwater species, it does not currently include NMFS marine and anadromous species data forcing agencies to rely on separate, manual processes. This program closes that gap by integrating marine and anadromous species data into the existing FWS platform, creating a single, unified experience for all ESA-listed species .

Peraton is seeking a Senior GIS Developer
to lead the production of federal species range maps for a high-priority data integration program. You will produce range maps for marine and anadromous taxa in compliance with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) Range Mapping Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), facilitating iterative review cycles with government SMEs and coordinating formal government sign-off.

Work Location:
Remote

Day to Day Responsibilities:

Lead species range map production, producing complete range maps for all marine and anadromous taxa in full compliance with the FWS Range Mapping Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
Obtain and review the FWS Range Mapping SOP at or before project kickoff
Conduct spatial data aggregation and normalization of range data from cloud data platform outputs, applying CRS transformations and spatial format standardization
Validate spatial intersects against authoritative geographic layers, addressing dynamic habitat boundaries and overlapping Critical Habitat designations
Facilitate iterative range map review cycles with both FWS Ecological Services and NOAA Fisheries (National Marine Fisheries Service) SMEs, incorporating feedback and producing revised map versions
Produce QA documentation for each individual range map, ensuring all maps meet SOP acceptance criteria before submission for government sign-off
Coordinate FWS Ecological Services sign-off on the Range Map Set deliverable
Support the development of updated range maps post-production as part of operational handoff documentation

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

Bachelors degree and 8 years professional experience, or a Masters degree and 6 years professional experience, or an Associates degree and 10 years professional experience; or a high school diploma/equivalent and 12 years' professional experience.
U.S. Citizenship required; must have the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance; all work must be performed within the United States.
Extensive GIS experience with a focus on species range mapping or federal environmental applications.
Direct experience with FWS Range Mapping SOP or equivalent federal range mapping standards.
Proficiency in ArcGIS, QGIS, or equivalent GIS platforms.
Proficiency in Python for GIS automation and spatial data processing, including ArcPy or equivalent scripting libraries.
Proficiency in SQL for querying and validating spatial data within cloud data platforms.
Experience with coordinate reference system transformations and spatial data normalization.
Experience conducting spatial intersect validation and Critical Habitat analysis.
Strong QA documentation skills for geospatial deliverables

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with NOAA Fisheries marine or anadromous species range data.
Familiarity with Databricks or cloud data platforms for spatial data retrieval.
Experience coordinating formal government deliverable approvals.
GISP certification or equivalent.

Job Summary

UFV's Department of Planning, Geography and Environmental Studies (PGES) in the Faculty of Science invites applications for a tenure-track, open-rank Professor of Land-Use Planning with an interest in one or more of the following areas: sustainable development, food security, environmental, and Indigenous community planning. The successful applicant will join a thriving faculty that supports programs in Geography, Environmental Studies, and Geographic Information Systems (GIS). The Bachelor of Regional and Community Planning (BRCP) degree has recently been accredited and has strong enrollment. The successful candidate will help to further grow and strengthen the new planning program in PGES and contribute to practicums and professional experience, PGES programs’ curriculum development and teaching.

The successful candidate will teach undergraduate courses and supervise undergraduate research students through studio, applied practicum, and independent study courses. Teaching assignments may include Settlements(PLAN 160), Social Geography: The Urban Experience (GEOG 241), GIS for the Built Environment (GEOG 355), Quantitative Methods in Geography (GEOG 252), Planning Law (PLAN 310) and Indigenous Land Use and Community Planning (PLAN 410), but the final list will be tailored to the expertise of the successful candidate. In addition to teaching, the successful candidate will actively participate in PGES activities, service, events, and initiatives, and will be committed to ongoing professional development.

PGES seeks a collegial and energetic individual with exceptional communication skills, demonstrated excellence in teaching at the undergraduate level, and experience in teaching across traditional disciplinary boundaries and delivering courses in community settings. The successful candidate is expected to build relationships with Fraser Valley municipalities and Indigenous communities by providing students with collaborative and integrative applied experiential learning opportunities. Incorporating Indigenous perspectives in the curriculum is essential, as is teaching international students and managing the needs of students in a diverse learning environment.

Short-listed applicants will have an emerging record of applied research or professional productivity commensurate with their experience. The ability to attract external funding and establish a successful applied research program at UFV to support research and student learning experiences are highly desirable. The ability to use Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Remote Sensing, statistical software (SPSS/STATA), and emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence to support land-use planning will be an asset, as is experience with community outreach in agricultural regions with rapidly growing urban centers.

Qualifications

Extensive knowledge of land-use planning: urban spatial structure and physical design within urban and regional settings.
A master’s degree in urban and regional planning or a closely related field from a recognized post-secondary institution is required, in addition to extensive professional experience. However, a PhD in the mentioned disciplines is preferred.
Registered Professional Planner certification with the Canadian Institute of Planners, facilitated by the Planning Standards Board of Canada, is required .
Teaching experience at the undergraduate level with recent evidence of teaching excellence is preferred.
Familiarity with technology-supported teaching both in the classroom, online and in the planning profession.
Effective cross-cultural, interdisciplinary communication skills and experience working with Indigenous communities are assets.
A growing list of impactful applied research and/or community-based planning initiatives.
Interest in service contribution to PGES, UFV, and Indigenous communities of the Fraser Valley.

How to Apply

To be considered for this position, please submit a complete application package that includes a cover letter, curriculum vitae, teaching philosophy statement, research interest statement, samples of scholarly activities (e.g., publication or project portfolio), and three letters of reference. In your application, please indicate your eligibility to work legally in Canada.

Applications will be reviewed by the SAC in December 2026, however the posting will be kept open for applications until the end of January 2027.

You will receive a confirmation email once you successfully apply for the position. If not, do not hesitate to contact the Njoyn Help Desk at candidate.njoynhelp@cgi.com or 1-877-427-7717, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. (EST).

UFV is committed to equity in employment, and all qualified candidates are encouraged to apply; however, Canadians and permanent residents will be given priority. UFV will contact only candidates receiving an interview. Shortlisted applicants may be required to undergo a criminal record check and a verification of their education credentials.

For further information about the position, please contact Dr. Cherie Enns, RPP, Chair, Bachelor of Regional and Community Planning, University of the Fraser Valley, at cherie.enns@ufv.ca.

About UFV

The University of the Fraser Valley is located on the traditional territory of the Halq'eméylem-speaking peoples. We express our gratitude and respect for the honour of living and working in Stó:lo Tém:éxw (Stó:lo Land; Stó:lo World). In all that we do, UFV strives to support and honour the Stó:lo peoples goals of self-determination and well-being on these lands. UFV has campus locations in Abbotsford, Chilliwack, Mission, and Hope in the beautiful British Columbia, and in Chandigarh, India. Recognized as one of BC's top employers, UFV offers a combination of career and lifestyle benefits. Join a team of 1,400 passionate professionals who value integrity, inclusivity and excellence. At UFV, you will serve a vibrant community and shape the future of 15,000 students.

Indigenization, equity, and diversity are essential to our work as a university. A diverse community fosters the inclusion of voices that have been historically underrepresented and marginalized. Purpose

Serve as a technical resource supporting and coordinating SMUD’s projects, environmental programs and regulatory requirements, including:
Plan, develop, implement, and evaluate environmental programs;
Work with contractors and consultants;
Train business unit personnel in environmental procedures;
Ensure work quality and accuracy as it relates to environmental issues;
Ensure compliance with applicable environmental rules, policies, regulations, and procedures.

Flex classifications (that permit progression from lower-level classes to higher level classes without examination based upon assessment of an individual's experience and performance) within the series:

Entry
: Incumbent acquires knowledge, skills and abilities to perform the tasks associated within the series but are not yet demonstrating these at the Journey level.
Journey

Prepare, review and submit permit applications, technical reports, and compliance documentation in a timely and accurate manner.
Monitor organizational activities for compliance and recommend corrective actions as needed.

Interpret environmental data and prepare detailed technical reports, summaries, and recommendations.
Provide technical expertise to support decision-making and project planning.
Environmental Education and Training

Promote environmental awareness within the organization and community through presentations, workshops, and educational materials.
Project Management

Manage or serve as a key contributor to environmental projects and initiatives, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate with cross-functional teams to integrate environmental considerations into project planning, design and implementation.
Track project milestones, budgets and deliverables, ensuring successful project outcomes.
Sustainability Initiatives

Identify opportunities to reduce the organization’s environmental footprint and improve sustainability practices.
Develop strategies, track progress, and report on sustainability metrics and goals.
Community Engagement

Represent the organization in meetings with regulatory agencies, community organizations, and external partners.
Facilitate public outreach, engagement and education efforts on environmental issues and programs.
Emergency Response Preparedness

Develop and maintain response plans for environmental emergencies such as spills, releases or contamination events.
Participate in drills, training, and incident response activities to ensure organizational readiness.
Research and Monitoring

Stay current on emerging environmental regulations, policies and technologies and evaluate their potential impacts on organizational operations.
Conduct research and prepare recommendations for program or policy updates.
Grant Writing and Funding Acquisition

Research and identify funding opportunities to support environmental programs and initiatives.
Prepare grant proposals and manage awarded projects to ensure compliance with funding requirements.
Collaboration and Communication

Serve as a liaison between departments, leadership, regulatory agencies, and community stakeholders on environmental issues.
Clearly communicate technical information, both orally and in writing, to diverse audiences including non-technical staff and the public.

Methods and techniques for report preparation and writing;
Techniques and practices for problem research and resolution;
Methods and techniques for record keeping;
Standard operating procedures for modern office equipment including a computer and applicable software;
English grammar, punctuation and vocabulary standards.

Skills To

Conduct environmental audits, inspections and assessments;
Interpret, assess and apply pertinent policies, procedures, regulations, and requirements relative to environmental fields;
Promote regulatory awareness among business unit managers;
Recommend changes to work processes to reduce risk and work closely with others to implement changes;

Establish and maintain effective working relationships internally/externally.

Experience working with regulatory agencies, permitting process and environmental compliance programs.
Knowledge of CEQA, federal and state endangered species regulations, and habitat conservation plans.

Overview

CARRERAS PARA SONREÍR

En PepsiCo, descubrirás un lugar donde nuestra misión es crear sonrisas alrededor del mundo. Con más de 500 marcas queridas, incluyen Gatorade, Lay's y Quaker y nuestro trabajo llega a millones de personas cada día.

En el corazón de nuestra compañía hay un equipo de pensadores y creadores que colaboran para innovar y convertir las ideas en acciones. Impulsados por la innovación y centrados en crear momentos de alegría a través de los alimentos y bebidas, nuestras decisiones se guían por y para el consumidor, creando oportunidades para que nuestros asociados realicen un trabajo significativo y tengan un impacto duradero en las comunidades a las que servimos.

Sea cual sea tu función, formarás parte de una comunidad global que valora tus ideas y te empodera para que tengas impacto en tu carrera y en el mundo que te rodea.

Responsibilities

La oportunidad

Liderar la estrategia regional de Seguridad, Salud Ocupacional y Sustentabilidad (EHS)
para las operaciones de Chile, Argentina, Uruguay y Paraguay con alcance en plantas, centros de distribución, sucursales y flota.

Gestionar riesgos críticos y fortalecer la prevención de incidentes, asegurando el cumplimiento del marco regulatorio de seguridad, salud ocupacional y medioambiente en los tres países. Liderar la agenda de sustentabilidad en materia de agua, energía, emisiones, residuos y envases, traduciendo los compromisos corporativos en planes de acción medibles.

Liderar y desarrollar al equipo regional de EHS, así como asesorar al liderazgo de Operaciones en decisiones relacionadas con la seguridad de las personas, la continuidad operacional y los riesgos regulatorios. Impulsar una cultura preventiva integrada en la operación y orientada a la reducción sostenible de riesgos críticos.

Tu impacto

Define la estrategia regional de seguridad, salud ocupacional y sustentabilidad, y responde por su ejecución en plantas, centros de distribución, sucursales y flota de Chile, Argentina y Uruguay.
Asegura el cumplimiento del marco legal de seguridad, salud y medioambiente en los tres países, incluidos la gestión preventiva exigida a la organización, los protocolos de vigilancia de la salud y el control documental y en terreno de empresas contratistas.
Gestiona la relación con autoridades y organismos administradores: permisos, autorizaciones sectoriales, reportes regulatorios y atención de fiscalizaciones, respondiendo por su oportunidad y exactitud.
Conduce la investigación de accidentes e incidentes de alto potencial, valida las causas raíz y verifica el cierre efectivo de los planes de acción.
Lidera la agenda de sustentabilidad de la operación —agua, energía, emisiones, y residuos —, traduciendo los compromisos corporativos en metas por sitio con responsables y plazos.
Define el modelo de formación en seguridad y salud, y responde por su cobertura y por el cumplimiento de las horas de formación exigidas por la normativa.
Lidera el equipo regional de seguridad, salud y medioambiente, y administra el presupuesto del área.
Reporta el desempeño del área al equipo de liderazgo de Operaciones y a la organización regional, mediante indicadores de exposición y de avance de los planes de control, no únicamente de accidentabilidad ocurrida.

Qualifications

¿A quién buscamos?

Position Description

JOB DESCRIPTION

Would you like to have a career with a collaborative, diverse, and dynamic mining company? We have an exciting opportunity for you!

Barrick is looking for a Geospatial Data & GIS Solutions Lead. The successful candidate is responsible for supporting and advancing geospatial data, GIS, remote sensing, data integration and technical automation capabilities across Exploration. The role works at the intersection of geoscience, GIS, remote sensing, data management and development, helping ensure geological, geochemical, geophysical, remote-sensing and other Exploration datasets are appropriately captured, organized, integrated, quality-controlled, accessible and reusable.

The role combines strong geospatial expertise with hands-on technical development, including the use of Python and geospatial technologies to improve, automate and standardize workflows. Working closely with the Regional Geosciences Data & Analytics Manager and multidisciplinary Exploration teams, the role will help strengthen data standards and knowledge continuity, integrate GIS with other Exploration systems, and develop practical, reusable solutions. The successful candidate is not expected to be an expert in every technology; the role requires a strong geospatial and technical foundation, hands-on Python capability, collaborative problem solving and a strong orientation toward continuous learning. This position is located in Toronto, Canada. The yearly salary for this position is between CAD 119,000 – 133,000.

At Barrick, our vision is to be the world’s most valued gold mining business by finding, developing, and operating the best assets with the best people. We are committed to a safe work environment sending every person home safe and healthy every day and leaving a sustainable legacy on our host communities.

Responsibilities

Work with geological, geochemical, geophysical, remote-sensing and other Exploration datasets across GIS, databases, project environments and web-based platforms.
Support and improve workflows using ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Enterprise, ArcGIS Online, Web GIS, Field Maps and Survey123.
Compile, integrate, QA/QC and standardize geospatial and geoscience datasets; improve how spatial data is structured, documented, discovered, shared and reused.
Help establish practical geospatial data standards, metadata, naming conventions and reusable project structures aligned with corporate standards and protocols.
Work with raster, satellite and remote-sensing datasets; process, analyze, integrate and visualize them alongside geological, geochemical and geophysical information.
Use Python to automate repetitive geospatial and data-processing workflows and develop scripts, tools and lightweight solutions for GIS, compilation, QA/QC, analysis and integration.
Use ArcPy and other geospatial Python libraries where appropriate, and work with SQL, APIs and spatial databases to connect GIS with other Exploration data systems.
Identify manual or repetitive workflows and determine opportunities to simplify, standardize or automate them before introducing new technology.
Participate in Git/version-control and modern development practices and collaborate with data engineering and analytics/development specialists to move useful prototypes into reliable operational workflows.
Use approved AI-assisted development tools responsibly where they can improve development, learning, documentation or workflow efficiency.
Work directly with geologists, geochemists, geophysicists, GIS/geoscience data specialists, data engineers and analytics/development resources to understand requirements and co-create practical solutions.
Document datasets, systems and workflows; support knowledge transfer so important technical knowledge is reusable and understood by the broader team.
Support field and office-based Exploration workflows and travel to projects or regional offices as required.
Promote continuous improvement in GIS, geospatial data management, integration and automation practices.
Comply with Barrick Health & Safety, Code of Conduct, Human Rights, Environmental and Community Relations requirements and applicable company policies.

Qualifications

Academic degree in Geography, GIS/Geomatics, Geospatial Science, Remote Sensing, Computer Science, Geoscience, Geological Engineering, Surveying or a related technical discipline required
Strong understanding of GIS and geospatial data concepts and practices, with hands-on experience using professional GIS technologies, preferably the Esri ecosystem required
Experience working with both vector and raster geospatial datasets, including remote sensing, satellite imagery or raster processing required
Hands-on Python programming experience, preferably applied to geospatial data processing, analysis, automation or development preferred
Strong understanding of coordinate systems, projections, spatial data quality, QA/QC and sound data-management practices preferred
Experience compiling, managing, standardizing or integrating geospatial datasets preferred
Strong analytical and practical problem-solving skills, including the ability to understand existing workflows and user needs before selecting a technical solution preferred
Ability to communicate and collaborate effectively with technical and non-technical users across multidisciplinary Exploration teams preferred
Strong orientation toward continuous learning and improvement; ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with the broader team preferred
Valuable but not all required: ArcPy, SQL/SQL Server, spatial databases, APIs, FME/ETL, Git, Azure DevOps, ArcGIS Enterprise/Online, Web GIS, Field Maps, Survey123, cloud geospatial technologies, data pipelines, Leapfrog, Geosoft, Power BI, geoscience/mining data, machine learning or AI-assisted development preferred
Experience in mineral exploration, mining, geology, geophysics, geochemistry, remote sensing or natural resources is highly valuable; strong candidates from other geospatial or scientific backgrounds preferred
Eligible to live and work in the applicable country required
Availability for occasional travel to Exploration projects and regional offices required

What We Can Offer You

A comprehensive compensation package including a competitive medical, dental, and vision plan with national provider networks, a 401k retirement plan with employer contribution, paid time off, company-sponsored medical clinics, company match share purchase program, and much more!
Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team.
Opportunities to grow and learn with the industry colleagues are endless.
Access to a variety of career opportunities across the organization.
Barrick is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer

Thank you for your application, however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

new_jobs.description:
About Peraton

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world's leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we're keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Program Overview

The program is an IDIQ contract for an AWS-based cloud hosting system. Currently, Peraton is supporting the Cloud Security, IoT, and AIML use cases for the environment in a hybrid work environment with Federal employees. Peraton also support the following applications as part of the environment: Dremio, Tableau, Globus, Posit/RStudio, Atlassian, ThingLogix, Alteryx and CloudCheckr.

About The Role

Peraton's Department of the Interior (DOI), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), and NOAA's National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) have identified a critical gap in the federal government's ability to conduct comprehensive Endangered Species Act (ESA) research. While FWS operates an authoritative web-based platform for managing data for terrestrial and freshwater species, it does not currently include NMFS marine and anadromous species data forcing agencies to rely on separate, manual processes. This program closes that gap by integrating marine and anadromous species data into the existing FWS platform, creating a single, unified experience for all ESA-listed species .

Peraton is seeking a Senior GIS Developer
to lead the production of federal species range maps for a high-priority data integration program. You will produce range maps for marine and anadromous taxa in compliance with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) Range Mapping Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), facilitating iterative review cycles with government SMEs and coordinating formal government sign-off.

Work Location:
Remote

Day to Day Responsibilities:

Lead species range map production, producing complete range maps for all marine and anadromous taxa in full compliance with the FWS Range Mapping Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
Obtain and review the FWS Range Mapping SOP at or before project kickoff
Conduct spatial data aggregation and normalization of range data from cloud data platform outputs, applying CRS transformations and spatial format standardization
Validate spatial intersects against authoritative geographic layers, addressing dynamic habitat boundaries and overlapping Critical Habitat designations
Facilitate iterative range map review cycles with both FWS Ecological Services and NOAA Fisheries (National Marine Fisheries Service) SMEs, incorporating feedback and producing revised map versions
Produce QA documentation for each individual range map, ensuring all maps meet SOP acceptance criteria before submission for government sign-off
Coordinate FWS Ecological Services sign-off on the Range Map Set deliverable
Support the development of updated range maps post-production as part of operational handoff documentation

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

Bachelors degree and 8 years professional experience, or a Masters degree and 6 years professional experience, or an Associates degree and 10 years professional experience; or a high school diploma/equivalent and 12 years' professional experience.
U.S. Citizenship required; must have the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance; all work must be performed within the United States.
Extensive GIS experience with a focus on species range mapping or federal environmental applications.
Direct experience with FWS Range Mapping SOP or equivalent federal range mapping standards.
Proficiency in ArcGIS, QGIS, or equivalent GIS platforms.
Proficiency in Python for GIS automation and spatial data processing, including ArcPy or equivalent scripting libraries.
Proficiency in SQL for querying and validating spatial data within cloud data platforms.
Experience with coordinate reference system transformations and spatial data normalization.
Experience conducting spatial intersect validation and Critical Habitat analysis.
Strong QA documentation skills for geospatial deliverables

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with NOAA Fisheries marine or anadromous species range data.
Familiarity with Databricks or cloud data platforms for spatial data retrieval.
Experience coordinating formal government deliverable approvals.
GISP certification or equivalent.

Details

Target Salary Range: $66,000 - $106,000. This represents the typical salary range for this position. Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual's experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay.

Benefits Statement: Peraton offers eligible employees a variety of benefits including medical, dental, vision, life, health savings account, short/long term disability, EAP, parental leave, 401(k), paid time off (PTO) for vacation, and company paid holidays. A full listing of available benefits can be viewed at https://www.careers.peraton.com/benefits.

Application Statements: The application period for the job is estimated to be 30 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. By applying to this job, you are expressing interest in the role and the Company. During the review of your application, you may be required to participate in an on-camera interview, as well as participate in a process to verify your identity. Use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools of any kind during Peraton interviews is strictly prohibited unless the candidate has obtained prior written authorization. All interview responses must be the candidate's own.

Who We Are

KPA helps automotive businesses keep their people safe, protect their operations, and stay ahead of regulatory change with our 3 Pillars for Complete Compliance: Software, Consulting, and Training. Since 1986, KPA has helped automotive businesses navigate the complexities of compliance.

Named as one of Built In Colorado’s Best Places to Work for seven years in a row, KPA is made up of talented individuals working together for the greater good. We’re here to help our clients build safe, thriving organizations, and we’re looking for people with a common goal to help us do it.

Position Description
:

As a member of the Risk Management team, the EHS Risk Management Consultant will play a crucial role in developing and maintaining strong relationships with clients to establish and demonstrate exceptional industry and regulatory knowledge through onsite field audits, employee trainings, and regulatory interaction. The objective of an EHS Risk Management Consultant is to minimize risk to increase profitability for the client. This position develops and maintains relationships with regional clients, potential clients, dealer group management, and state dealer associations. A professional, likable, persuasive, and customer service-oriented demeanor is essential for success.

Location:

While this is a remote position based out of the employee’s home office, it will require frequent visits to clients within the territory, including roughly 1-2 weeks of overnight travel per quarter. The candidate for this role will either be based in Baton Rouge or Lafayette, LA servicing clients across the state.

In the first 30 days you will:

Inherit a customer service base and immediately establish relationships with Mangers and Management teams across many different businesses

In the first 60 days you will:

Complete new hire orientation training to be fully operational as a KPA Risk Management Consultant

In the first 6 months you will:

Establish and demonstrate exceptional industry and regulatory knowledge through onsite field audits, employee training, and regulatory interaction
Organize a quarterly visit schedule to maximize travel efficiency based on local and distant client groupings and service frequency
Assist with and/or prepare various compliance documentation as needed (i.e., Hazard Communication, Respiratory Protection, Tier II reporting, OSHA 300 logs, Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) ID numbers, tank permitting, and Spill Prevention Control & Countermeasures (SPCC) Plans)

By the end of the first year you will:

Assist in developing, implementing, and monitoring accident prevention programs, policies, and procedures to ensure continuous safe working conditions in accordance with State, Federal, and Local laws and regulations to assist the client in striving to achieve Zero Accident / lost time injuries
Help communicate and implement environmental management compliance systems
Support the ongoing growth of the company by performing exceptional customer service, documenting and submitting 20 referrals or sales leads per year to your area Account Executive
Responsible for promoting productive relationships with dealer group management for KPA clients and State Dealer Association Management. Maintains effective internal and external public relations
Performs other duties and fulfills other responsibilities, as assigned

As an EHS Risk Management Consultant, you are expected to develop and maintain internal and external relationships with:

Regional Director, Regional Managers, Field Office Manager, staff colleagues, and other members of KPA management team
District clients, potential clients, dealer group management and state dealer associations
Regional Clients

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science/Engineering, Safety Studies, or related disciplines preferred
Three years of Environmental Health & Safety experience preferred

Ability to seek out and communicate effectively with senior management and stakeholders at our client organizations
Proven background in building and working with collaborative teams
Ability to meet deadlines, multi-task and effectively and professionally deal with customers and external contacts to the Company
Strong leadership and problem-solving skills. Ability to work independently
Strong computer skills, including familiarity with word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, Microsoft Outlook, and phone/tablet applications
Must have the ability to travel overnight a total of around 1-2 weeks per quarter

Physical Requirements:

Physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Active driver’s license and insurance as required by law
Reliable transportation and ability to drive between client visits, typically 4 days per week. Driving time per day varies according to geography and scheduling

Ability to sufficiently receive audio signals to proceed with caution around heavy machinery, vehicles and other warning noises to ensure safety

Ability to stay overnight in a hotel a total multiple weeks per quarter and fly on an airplane domestically.

Annual base salary range between $55-70k

Position Title

Fish Screening, Passage and Restoration Coordinator (Natural Resource Specialist 2)

Job Description

Help the Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife fulfill its mission:
To protect and enhance Oregon's fish and wildlife and their habitats for use and enjoyment by present and future generations.

We are hiring for one full-time, permanent position located in Klamath Falls, Oregon.

What You Will Do

In this role, you will be tasked with advancing ODFW priorities for fish screening, fish passage and aquatic restoration efforts in the Klamath Watershed. The position is a critical liaison between project proponents, the fish screening program, fish passage program and Habitat Division. You will be responsible for outreach and providing technical assistance to irrigation districts, water users, watershed councils and conservation groups in the Klamath Basin. Additionally, you will perform data collection, analysis, and evaluation for potential fish screening and passage projects and associated habitat restoration projects, as well as project coordination. You will be part of the Klamath Watershed District and as such, will have the opportunity to participate in a wide range of other fish, wildlife, and habitat related activities throughout the Klamath Basin.

This position will also require the successful candidate to either possess or obtain an All-Terrain Vehicle Safety Education card and a Boater Education Card within the first 6 months of hire.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. They are not an exhaustive list of all responsibilities and duties required.

For a full review of the position details, duties, and working conditions, please review the position description located here.

Clearly describe how you meet the desired attributes in your application materials. We cannot accept additional application materials after the application deadline. These materials determine whether you move forward in the selection process and help establish your starting salary. Be sure your work and education history is accurate, thorough, and fully reflects your skills and experience, even if they do not seem directly related to the position. Click here to learn more about
Equal Pay Analysis
and
What You Need to Know to Get the Job

Minimum Qualifications

What we are looking for:

To be considered for this position, applicants must meet one of the following options:

Option 1: Six years of biological experience performing studies, research, or resource management activities in a fish or wildlife program that included one year of at least two of the following: gathering data, analyzing data, or preparing reports
Option 2: Two years of biological experience performing studies, research, or resource management activities in a fish or wildlife program that included one year of at least two of the following: gathering data, analyzing data, or preparing reports, AND a Bachelor's degree in Fisheries or Wildlife Science, or a closely related Bachelor’s degree with at least 45 quarter (30 semester) hours of biological/ecological coursework
Option 3: One year biological experience performing studies, research, or resource management activities in a fish or wildlife program that included at least two of the following: gathering data, analyzing data, or preparing reports, AND a Master's degree Fisheries or Wildlife Science, or a closely related Master’s degree in biological/ecological sciences
Option 4: A Doctorate degree in Fisheries or Wildlife Science, or a closely related Doctorate degree in biological/ecological sciences.

Note: Applicants who have obtained a Master’s degree or Doctorate that included work experience from an internship, work/study, thesis, or similar program may list this experience in their application to receive credit for the work experience. The Master’s degree/Doctorate and applicable work experience will be considered separately, and both the education and applicable experience may count toward minimum qualifications.

Desired Attributes

Proven experience collaborating with other entities which may include: Tribes, watershed councils, non-governmental organizations, water users, and private landowners to advance fish and/or wildlife habitat projects.
Experience in providing technical expertise for fish, wildlife, or habitat related projects.
Experience implementing aquatic or riparian restoration projects.
Proven ability to build and maintain successful interagency, Tribal, and non-governmental partnerships.
Excellent public speaking, writing, and outreach abilities.
Ability to use persuasive diplomacy while working with landowners, partner agencies, and the public.
Experience with fish passage and screening technology and solutions.

Application Details and Instructions

The State of Oregon does not request or require your age, date of birth, attendance or graduation dates from an educational institution during the application process.
The salary listed is the non-PERS qualifying salary range. If the successful candidate is PERS qualifying, the salary range will reflect an additional 6.95%.
This recruitment will be used to establish a list of qualified people to fill the current vacancy and may be used to fill other vacancies as they occur.
State of Oregon Employees, must apply through their employee Workday account.
Please save a copy of this job announcement for reference, as it is not available for you to view after the announcement deadline.
First time applying to the State of Oregon? Consider utilizing a WorkSource Oregon Resource event! You can also view this video or this knowledge article for assistance.
Reasonable accommodation for interviews will be provided upon request to individuals with disabilities.
The job posting closes at 11:59 PM (PDT/PST) on the close date. After you submit your application, be sure to respond to the two questionnaires relating to public records requests and veterans’ preference immediately following your submittal. These questions are necessary to complete the application process
If you are experiencing difficulty applying for this position or have questions, please call 503.947.6051 and ask to speak to a recruiter.

Benefits Of Joining Our Team

ODFW is dedicated to cultivating a diverse and inclusive workforce as we strive to represent and better serve our neighboring communities. Our most important asset is our employees, and each person brings unique, different, and important contributions to the workplace and community we serve. With Oregon’s changing demographics, a workforce that reflects this change will make us stronger and create an opportunity for better decision making.

To learn more about the agency and the work we do, view the following video at https://myodfw.com/about

If you enjoy the outdoors, Oregon is the place for you. We have glaciated mountain peaks to the east, the Pacific Ocean to the west and the massive Columbia River Gorge to the north. You can fish 365 days a year, and there is hunting for big game, waterfowl, and game birds. Overview

CARRERAS PARA SONREÍR

En PepsiCo, descubrirás un lugar donde nuestra misión es crear sonrisas alrededor del mundo. Con más de 500 marcas queridas, incluyen Gatorade, Lay's y Quaker y nuestro trabajo llega a millones de personas cada día.

En el corazón de nuestra compañía hay un equipo de pensadores y creadores que colaboran para innovar y convertir las ideas en acciones. Impulsados por la innovación y centrados en crear momentos de alegría a través de los alimentos y bebidas, nuestras decisiones se guían por y para el consumidor, creando oportunidades para que nuestros asociados realicen un trabajo significativo y tengan un impacto duradero en las comunidades a las que servimos.

Sea cual sea tu función, formarás parte de una comunidad global que valora tus ideas y te empodera para que tengas impacto en tu carrera y en el mundo que te rodea.

Responsibilities

La oportunidad

Liderar la estrategia regional de Seguridad, Salud Ocupacional y Sustentabilidad (EHS)
para las operaciones de Chile, Argentina, Uruguay y Paraguay con alcance en plantas, centros de distribución, sucursales y flota.

Gestionar riesgos críticos y fortalecer la prevención de incidentes, asegurando el cumplimiento del marco regulatorio de seguridad, salud ocupacional y medioambiente en los tres países. Liderar la agenda de sustentabilidad en materia de agua, energía, emisiones, residuos y envases, traduciendo los compromisos corporativos en planes de acción medibles.

Liderar y desarrollar al equipo regional de EHS, así como asesorar al liderazgo de Operaciones en decisiones relacionadas con la seguridad de las personas, la continuidad operacional y los riesgos regulatorios. Impulsar una cultura preventiva integrada en la operación y orientada a la reducción sostenible de riesgos críticos.

Tu impacto

Define la estrategia regional de seguridad, salud ocupacional y sustentabilidad, y responde por su ejecución en plantas, centros de distribución, sucursales y flota de Chile, Argentina y Uruguay.
Asegura el cumplimiento del marco legal de seguridad, salud y medioambiente en los tres países, incluidos la gestión preventiva exigida a la organización, los protocolos de vigilancia de la salud y el control documental y en terreno de empresas contratistas.

Define el modelo de formación en seguridad y salud, y responde por su cobertura y por el cumplimiento de las horas de formación exigidas por la normativa.
Lidera el equipo regional de seguridad, salud y medioambiente, y administra el presupuesto del área.
Reporta el desempeño del área al equipo de liderazgo de Operaciones y a la organización regional, mediante indicadores de exposición y de avance de los planes de control, no únicamente de accidentabilidad ocurrida.

Qualifications

¿A quién buscamos?

Formación en Ingeniería Industrial, Química, Ambiental, Mecánica o carrera afín.
Más de 10 años de experiencia liderando Seguridad, Salud Ocupacional y Medio Ambiente (EHS) en operaciones industriales, manufactura, logística o distribución. Experiencia en la industria de alimentos y bebidas será considerada un plus.
Más de 4 años de experiencia liderando equipos EHS a nivel país o regional, idealmente equipos multiculturales y distribuidos en diferentes países.
Experiencia sólida en gestión de riesgos críticos, prevención de fatalidades, investigación de incidentes y análisis de causa raíz.
Conocimiento y experiencia en gestión de contratistas y cumplimiento regulatorio en materia de seguridad, salud ocupacional y medioambiente en entornos multinacionales.
Experiencia en implementación y auditoría de sistemas ISO 45001 e ISO 14001.
Conocimiento en gestión ambiental operacional, incluyendo agua, energía, residuos, emisiones y sustentabilidad.
Experiencia liderando procesos de transformación cultural y/o regulatoria en EHS.
Inglés avanzado.
Disponibilidad para viajar entre 30% y 40% del tiempo dentro de la región SoCo.
Deseable: Posgrado en Gestión, Sustentabilidad, Salud Ocupacional o área relacionada.
Deseable: Registro o certificación como Experto en Prevención de Riesgos, de acuerdo con la normativa local.

The Environmental Compliance Specialist will gain hands-on experience in environmental compliance processes while working under the guidance of senior Environmental Compliance professionals.

Helps prepare and submit permit applications, compliance reports, and environmental documentation.

Field Monitoring and Data Collection

Conducts site visits and field assessments to monitor environmental conditions and ensure regulatory adherence.
Collects and analyzes environmental data/samples related to air, water, and soil quality.
Assists in implementing best management practices (BMPs) for erosion control, stormwater management, and other environmental protections.

Trouble-shoot site compliance and BMP issues.

Reporting and Documentation

Maintains, organizes, and prepares environmental records, monitoring/inspection logs, and field notes.
Supports teams with environmental impact mitigation planning and tracking.

Project Coordination and Communication

Participates in team meetings and project discussions to provide regulatory insight.
